entries: Velocity is speed with a direction: the athlete covers 100 metres in 20 seconds for a speed of 5 metres per second, and running right makes it a velocity of 5 metres per second rightwards.
slots.label: Velocity
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: Distance-time graphs: the line climbs 120 metres in 60 seconds and the gradient triangle builds beneath it - gradient is rise over run, 120 over 60, a speed of 2 metres per second.
slots.label: Distance-time graphs
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: Velocity-time graphs: the line rises from 0 to 20 metres per second in 10 seconds, so the slope is an acceleration of 2 metres per second squared, while the shaded area growing under the line is the 100 metres travelled.
slots.label: Velocity-time graphs
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: Check the thinking: the runner covers 800 metres in 100 seconds for a speed of 8 metres per second, but ends at the start, so displacement and velocity are both zero.
slots.label: Check the thinking
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: Distance travelled per unit time, calculated as distance divided by time, measured in metres per second.
slots.label: Speed
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: Speed with a direction: displacement divided by time, so a round trip back to the start has zero average velocity.
slots.label: Velocity
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: The straight-line change in position from start to finish, with a direction - not the total path length.
slots.label: Displacement
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: The rate of change of velocity, read off a velocity-time graph as its gradient.
slots.label: Acceleration
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: Rise over run on a graph: on a distance-time graph it is the speed, and on a velocity-time graph it is the acceleration.
slots.label: Gradient
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: The product of velocity and time accumulated under the line, which equals the distance travelled.
slots.label: Area under a velocity-time graph
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.
